title: Protocol to assess the effect of disease-driving variants on mouse brain morphology and primary hippocampal neurons
protocol: Prepare the following items:
Fill the required number of 20 mL vials (one vial per brain) with about 10 mL of 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA).
Prepare the tubing system as in Figure 1A, attaching to one end of the tube a 27G needle.
Pull the skin taut before making a small incision just large enough to insert scissors and enlarge the gap.
Cut through the diaphragm along the rib cage until you see the heart.
Insert the needle into the left ventricle of the heart.
Make a small incision on the right atrium.
Fill the tubing system connected to the peristaltic pump with 1× PBS until solution drops out steadily from the needle at a speed of 5 mL/min.
Weigh the mouse in order to calculate the amount of Avertin needed.
Anesthetize the mouse by intraperitoneal injection (IP) of 250 mg/kg of avertin.
Place the anesthetized mouse in a glass jar or quiet environment for several minutes.
Place the mouse on its back on a flat, raised surface.
Gently tape the mouse's paws to immobilize them.
Make an abdominal incision, avoiding damage to the liver.
Incise the diaphragm and along the rib cage to reveal the heart.
Bend the upper part of the rib cage to expose the heart.
Insert a pump needle into the left ventricle carefully without puncturing other parts of the heart.
Cut the right atrium while starting to pump PBS solution at 5 mL/min.
Continue perfusing with 1× PBS until the liver changes from dark to light brown and body structures turn white.
Perfuse with 15–20 mL of PBS.
Transfer the tube into a container with 4% PFA.
Resume pumping 15-20 mL of 4% PFA solution.
Stop the pump when paws and tail become inflexible.
Remove the needle from the heart, flush it with water, then refill with 1× PBS for the next animal.
Decapitate the mouse and cut the skin longitudinally from the neck to between the eyes.
Cut the skull starting from the occipital region to the nasal bones using scissors.
Make a cut between the left and right anterolateral corner of the frontal bone.
Use forceps to detach the right and left portion of the skull bone to reveal the brain.
Scoop the brain away using a spatula and place it in 10 mL of 4% PFA.
Wash the pump with RNase-free distilled water for 3–4 minutes to flush out residual 4% PFA.
Fill the pump with 1× PBS after washing.
Incubate the brain overnight in a solution of 4% PFA and 1× PBS at 4°C.
Change to a solution of 5% sucrose in 1× PBS and incubate for 1 hour at 4°C.
Change to a solution of 10% sucrose in water and incubate for 1 hour at 4°C, ensuring the brain sinks to the bottom of the vial.
Replace with a 20% sucrose in water solution and incubate from 2 hours to overnight (about 16 hours) until the brain sinks to the bottom of the vial.
Change to a 30% sucrose in water solution and continue incubation at 4°C until the brain sinks to the bottom of the vial, which may take longer than one day.
Remove the brain from the 30% sucrose solution and dry it as much as possible on a paper towel.
Place the dried brain into a freezing mold, cover with Tissue-Plus™ O.C.T. compound.
Place the freezing mold on a flat surface containing dry ice.
Take the frozen O.C.T. embedded brain out from the mold.
Section the brain on Leica CM3050S Cryostat at 30 μm thickness.
Mount sections on gelatin-subbed microscope glass slides or collect them in a 1× PBS solution in a 12 well plate with no more than 4–5 sections per well.
Prepare a 1× PBS solution with 0.02% of sodium azide for storing brain sections at 4°C for about 30 days if needed.
Dry-mount the slides on the Fisherbrand™ Slide Drying Bench (FisherScientific) at 60°C for several hours or at room temperature overnight.
Immerse mounted brain slides in 100% ethanol for 1–2 min.
Immerse slides in 95% ethanol for 1 min.
Immerse slides in 70% ethanol for 1 min.
Dip slides in distilled water for 2-3 dips.
Immerse glass slides in Cresyl violet solution for 2–3 minutes.
Dip slides in water for 2–3 times.
Submerge slides in 70% Ethanol for 1 minute.
Incubate slides in 95% Ethanol for 1 minute.
Treat slides with 100% Ethanol for 1 minute.
Immerse slides in Xylene for 1 minute.
Place 3–4 drops of Permount Mounting Medium on the slide.
Hold the slide at a slant and slowly move the coverslip from the bottom edge to the top.
Gently push the cover glass with finger.
Wipe the other side of the slide with a Kimwipe.
Allow slides to dry for at least 3 hours or overnight before imaging.
Coat one glass cover slip per well in a 12-well plate with 400 μL of coating medium.
Incubate coated coverslips at 37°C for 1 hour or overnight.
Remove the mouse's head and place it in a 10 cm petri dish filled with 5 mL of Hanks' balanced salt solution (HBSS) 1×.
Make a careful incision into the skin and skull, carefully remove the brain, and transfer it to a 10 cm plate with HBSS 1×.
Wash three times with 4 ml of sterile water.
Let dry open under the biosafety cabinet for at least 15 min before seeding.
Separate the two hemispheres.
Remove the midbrain and meninges.
Locate the hippocampus and dissect it using small forceps.
Pool four dissected hippocampi in a 15 mL conical tube with 5 mL HBSS 1×.
Aspirate HBSS 1× without disturbing the dissociated hippocampi.
Add 1.5 mL pre-warmed TrypLE to the tube.
Pipette up and down with a p1000 to mechanically dissociate the tissue.
Incubate at 37°C for 15–20 min.
Aspirate coating medium from the 12 well plate.
Wash the wells three times with sterile water.
Add plating media to all wells.
Remove TrypLE from the tube and add 5 mL HBSS 1× slowly.
Centrifuge at 800 g for 5 min.
Wash cells twice with HBSS 1×.
Add 750 μL pre-warmed plating medium to the cells.
Dissociate using a p1000 and a p200 pipette, pipetting up and down 15 times or until no cell clumps are visible.
Put cells through a 70 μm cell strainer collecting the cells in a 50 mL conical tube.
Transfer the filtered cells to a 1.7 mL Eppendorf tube.
Count the cells with a hemocytometer and adjust the volume to contain 0.5 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Plate approximately 3.5 × 10^5 cells per well in a 12-well plate.
On DIV1, remove plating media and replace it with 1 mL of growth medium.
On DIV4, replace half of the medium with fresh medium containing 10 μM final concentration of 5-Fluoro-2′-deoxyuridine/Uridine (FdU/U).
Repeat replacing half of the medium with fresh medium containing FdU/U every 2 days.
Prepare pEGFP-C1 and 3×HA-PUM1 plasmids by DIV9 using an endotoxin-free Plasmid Midi Kit.
At DIV9, check the quality of the plated neurons by observing them under a microscope.
For each transfection, prepare Solution A and Solution B in separate sterile microcentrifuge tubes according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Vortex Solution A while adding Solution B dropwise (usually takes 30 s–1 min per reaction).
Incubate the mixed A+B solution at 24°C–26°C for 30 min.
Gently add the A+B solution dropwise to wells of a 12-well plate containing coverslip-plated neurons.
Gently move the plate back and forth to evenly distribute the transfection solution.
Incubate the plate at 37°C in a 5% CO2 incubator for 8 h to overnight.
Replace the medium containing transfection solution with growth medium.
Assess transfection success by monitoring pEGFP fluorescence in neurons under a fluorescence microscope 24 hours later.
Aspirate growth medium and wash coverslip-plated neurons by adding ice-cold PBS at DIV14.
Add a solution of 4% PFA to fix the cells and incubate for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Aspirate the fixing solution and wash neurons twice with ice-cold PBS.
Add permeabilization/blocking solution to 12-well plates and incubate at room temperature for 1 hour.
Aspirate the permeabilization/blocking solution and wash neurons three times for 5 minutes each with ice-cold PBS.
Incubate with primary antibodies as follows.
Prepare 100 μL of primary antibody solution (anti-GFP diluted 1:1,000 and anti-HA diluted 1:100 in blocking solution) per coverslip.
Place a 100 μL drop of primary antibody solution on a parafilm-coated plate for each coverslip.
Retrieve the coverslips using forceps, place onto drops of primary antibody solution, and incubate at 4°C for 16 h.
Transfer the coverslip-plated neurons to wells of a 12-well plate filled with 1× PBS and wash three times for 10 min each time.
Incubate with secondary antibodies as follows.
Prepare 100 μL of secondary antibody solution (Goat-anti-mouse-Alexa 488 diluted 1:500) and Donkey-anti-goat-Alexa 594 diluted in 1:150 in blocking solution for each coverslip.
Place 100 μL drop of secondary antibody solution on a parafilm-coated plate for each coverslip.

Retrieve coverslips using forceps, place onto drops of secondary antibody solution, and incubate at 24°C–26°C for 1 h. Note: Cover the plate in aluminum foil after adding the secondary antibodies to avoid exposure to light.
Perform all further steps in as little light as possible.
Transfer the coverslip-plated neurons to wells of a 12-well plate filled with 1× PBS.
Wash the neurons three times for 10 min each time.
Prepare microscope slides and place a drop of VECTASHIELD antifade DAPI mounting medium on the surface of the slide.
Retrieve coverslips from the 12-well plate using forceps.
Place the coverslip with neurons facing down onto the prepared slide.
Seal each coverslip with transparent nail polish.
Acquire Z-stack images with parameter settings using a laser-scanning confocal microscope equipped with a 63× objective and Zen2.6 Software.
Generate maximum intensity projections for all captured Z-stack files.
Perform neuron tracing and Sholl analysis using Neurolucida 360.
